EMPIRE & ROUTES / 帝国与丝路
02 · Unification & exchange

秦汉帝国与丝绸之路Qin–Han empire and the Silk Roads

公元前221年，秦完成统一并推行标准化制度。随后的汉帝国扩展交通与边疆治理，绿洲、草原和海路网络把丝绸、马匹、作物、宗教与技术带向更远的地方。In 221 BCE, Qin unification introduced standardised systems. The later Han empire expanded transport and frontier administration, while oasis, steppe and maritime routes carried silk, horses, crops, religions and technologies across Eurasia.

04 · Standardisation

统一制度与标准化Unification and standardisation

制度
郡县、度量衡、车轨与文字
物质证据
标准量器、权与诏版

秦在统一后推行统一度量衡、车轨和书写规范，并用道路、邮驿与行政系统连接各地。标准化的重量和尺量让税收、工程、贸易与政令执行更容易协调。After unification, Qin promoted common weights, measures, axle widths and writing standards, linking regions through roads, postal stations and administration. Standard measures made taxation, engineering, trade and official communication easier to coordinate.

统一并不等于各地文化完全相同，但制度标准创造了新的共同尺度。 Unification did not erase regional cultures, but common standards created new shared scales of administration.

05 · Routes

汉朝交通与丝路网络Han transport and Silk Road networks

关键交通
河西走廊、绿洲路线与驿站
交流物
丝绸、马匹、玻璃、作物与观念

张骞出使西域后，汉朝与中亚各地建立了更稳定的联系。丝绸之路并非一条固定道路，而是由绿洲、草原、沙漠和海上航线组成的网络；马匹与交通能力也因此成为帝国治理的重要资源。After Zhang Qian's missions to the Western Regions, Han China developed more stable links with Central Asia. The Silk Roads were not one fixed road but a network of oasis, steppe, desert and maritime routes. Horses and transport were therefore important resources for imperial administration.

路线运输的不只是商品，也传递技术、宗教、艺术和生活方式。 Routes carried not only goods, but also technologies, religions, art and ways of life.

06 · Technology exchange

技术、信仰与远距离传播Technology, belief and long-distance transmission

传播
双向而非单向交流
例子
丝绸、造纸、冶铁、佛教与作物

跨区域网络改变了材料、技术和思想流动的方式。丝绸向西传播，外来作物、玻璃器和佛教等观念进入中国，造纸等工艺也在后续历史中向外传播。交流往往经过多站转译，而不是从一地直接到达另一地。Long-distance networks changed how materials, technologies and ideas moved. Silk travelled westward, while crops, glass and Buddhist ideas entered China; papermaking and other crafts later spread outward. Exchange usually involved many intermediaries rather than a direct journey between two places.

丝绸之路的意义在于连接多个地方系统，并让知识在反复翻译和使用中改变。 The Silk Roads connected many local systems and changed knowledge through repeated translation and use.

关键概念：标准化如何运作
KEY IDEA · STANDARDS AS INFRASTRUCTURE

统一重量、长度、文字和道路规格，使不同地区可以共享同一套测量、运输和行政语言。标准化减少交易成本，也让中央政令更容易落实；但它同时需要工匠、官吏、道路和强制力共同维持。Common weights, lengths, writing and road specifications let different regions share scales of measurement, transport and administration. Standards reduce transaction costs and make central policy easier to implement, but they also require craftspeople, officials, roads and enforcement to maintain.

延伸思考THINK FURTHER

统一度量衡、道路和行政语言，与丝路沿线的多站交流构成了两种不同尺度的连接。比较标准化网络和远距离贸易网络：它们分别怎样降低交流成本，又会带来哪些新的依赖？Common measures, roads and administrative language created one scale of connection, while the Silk Roads created another through multi-stage exchange. Compare standardisation and long-distance trade: how did each lower the cost of interaction, and what new dependencies did each create?
